findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:76 says provider-reported usage wins over estimates for the same completed call, and lines 223-225 require preflight estimate records to stay separate from final provider-reported records. But the JSONL shape at lines 86-107 only has per-line recordId plus provider.requestIdHash, which is unavailable for blocked preflight refusals or pre-provider estimates. That means ledger readers cannot mechanically correlate an estimate/refusal record with the later provider-reported record for the same call, so the preflight/postflight budget semantics are not implementable as written. Add a required stable call/attempt correlation id shared across estimate, blocked, and final provider records.

docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:84 defines the future ledger as append-only JSONL and lines 212-216 plan schema/writer APIs, but the execution plan never chooses a ledger path or classifies the file as a runtime artifact, process evidence, or another artifact class. Existing Lattice rules require runtime artifact paths to be registry-backed with gitignore/materialHash/repair semantics (AGENTS.md:67; docs/requirements/decisions/lifecycle-artifact-scope.md:45-48,65). Without that placement/registry decision, an implementer can create an unregistered/tracked JSONL ledger or accidentally make usage logs affect materialHash/gates. Add the intended path plus runtime-artifact-registry/gitignore/materialHash semantics, or explicitly state a different artifact class and why.
